column3: BSB follows the critical-text order “ten horns and seven heads.” “Blasphemous names” renders “names of blasphemy.”
“With the feet of a bear” recasts “and its feet like a bear’s”; “the beast” is added.
BSB follows the critical text with no “I saw.” “Appeared to be mortally wounded” renders “as slain to death”; “and followed” is added.
“Arrogant and blasphemous words” renders “great things and blasphemies.” BSB has “authority to act” and no “war” (πόλεμον).
BSB follows the critical text with “His tabernacle—those who dwell in heaven”; the Textus Receptus has “and those who dwell.” “To speak blasphemies” renders “unto blasphemies.”
“Was permitted” renders “there was given”; BSB follows the critical text with “people.”
BSB moves “from the foundation of the world” to “have not been written”; the Greek places it after “the Lamb who was slain.”
BSB follows the critical text with “is destined for captivity” and “is to die by the sword”; the Textus Receptus has “leads into captivity” and “kills with the sword.” BSB adds “a call for.”
“Exercised … caused” renders the present “exercises … makes”; “this beast” is added.
“The second beast” is added; “performed” renders the present ποιεῖ.
“On behalf of the first beast” renders “before the beast”; “deceived” renders the present πλανᾷ.
“Was permitted” renders “there was given”; “breath” renders πνεῦμα (“spirit”).
“Required … to receive” renders the present “causes … that they may give them.”
BSB adds “a call for”; “insight” renders νοῦν.
